items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: and he told the dog, no, and we became friends

ctx.x: Yes, and you could hear all these master things and this classic stuff and you -- listen, I knocked on that door. I wanted to know and this big man come in there and the dog wanted to take me out and he told the dog, no, and we became friends, and he told me (unintelligible) but I made a mistake (unintelligible)

And he says, because he was very secretive and he would sit and play that stuff that he---- harmony, big enough harmony, polyharmony but you didn't realize what it is, because he was playing music. You see, when music becomes complete, you don't realize what he's doing in there, because he's doing here, takes all of these surprises out of it. He may playing dissonance up here, but down here, he's got something to take all that surprise out. This is what you hear. You listen to these great pianistsand they be…
